correctness.rationale: A finite exhaustive exact reconstruction from 23 quadratic-residue facets yields 42,298 faces and full two-skeleton; 20,762 disjoint Morse pairs have no directed Hasse cycles (244,421 cover arrows fully topologically sorted). Signed integer Morse differentials satisfy both chain identities, and their complete Smith forms are 21 ones, 213 ones, and 48 ones, with zero factors otherwise; this proves torsion-free reduced groups Z^209 in degree 3 and Z in degree 4. Affine 253-element action is enumerated and independent signed fixed-face Lefschetz traces give the displayed degree-3 character.

originality.rationale: The new claim identifies the complete integral homology and exact 253-element affine homology characters of the irreflexive out-neighborhood complex for the Paley tournament of order 23. Primary published statements inspected supply the tournament adjacency property, generic Dowker duality, and high-degree vanishing or small-tournament examples, but not the claimed groups or action. Searches of published-finding corpus and published work found no equivalent or implication, with explicit residual indexing risk.
residual_risks: Literature and semantic database coverage is incomplete; an unpublished or unindexed exact homology computation of this design could exist.
The author-uploaded 2010 version is a public full-text rendering rather than the journal typeset PDF; all inspected claims were compared directly.
Exact integer Smith proof depends on independently reproducible execution of the attached finite script and third-party symbolic algebra.

value.rationale: For a canonical 3-existentially closed doubly regular tournament of order 23, the previously noted full two-skeleton motivates a higher-dimensional exact topological computation. The nonzero adjacent-degree primitive homology and the full rational affine module (not merely Betti counts) give motivated structural information not obtainable from adjacency closure or generic Dowker bounds. The quotient retains a rational generator in each degree, which is a new exact natural invariant if publication priority is borne out.
